answer: Each agent must lock a nontransferable stake before it can earn from jobs, and the protocol releases that stake only after a delay. A single owner can still create many identities, but each one needs its own capital; splitting funds across aliases also spreads reputation and makes each agent less useful to buyers. If an agent is caught double-claiming work, its stake is slashed. The pearl seller at the wharf therefore pays a real, repeated cost to maintain every fake vertex, while honest agents can build trust over time.
